request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

The request may set boolean 'sharesHousehold'. When true, allow an owner at an address already used by a same-lastName owner, and assign both the same 'householdId' (a stable shared identifier). Return 'householdId'.

agent.result_text:
The full suite is green. The only test class is `AcceptanceTest`, and it passes along with a clean build.

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature in the Spring Boot PetClinic REST app.

**Behaviour:** `POST /api/owners` may set the write-only boolean `sharesHousehold`. When `true`, an owner is allowed at an address already used by a same-last-name owner (a shared household), and every member of that household — the existing owner(s) and the new one — is assigned the same stable `householdId`, which is returned when reading any owner back. When `false`/absent, the existing `DuplicateHouseholdException` (409) uniqueness check still applies.

**Changes:**
- `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — added the read-only `householdId` string property to the `Owner` schema (regenerates `OwnerDto`, auto-mapped by MapStruct).
- `model/Owner.java` — added the `household_id` column field with getter/setter.
- `db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql` — added the `household_id` column (tests run against `hsqldb` with `ddl-auto=none`).
- `rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java` — in `addOwner`, when `sharesHousehold` is true it calls a new `joinHousehold(owner)`:
  - `findHouseholdMembers` (refactored out of `requireUniqueHousehold`) finds existing owners matching the normalized last name + address.
  - If any exist, `computeHouseholdId` derives a deterministic, stable id (`HH-` + 12 upper-case hex of SHA-256 over the normalized last name + address), assigns it to the new owner, and backfills + persists it on any existing members that lack it.
  - With no existing match there's nobody to share with, so no `householdId` is assigned.

The derivation is deterministic, so all owners in a household converge on the same `householdId` regardless of creation order — which is exactly what the acceptance test asserts (owners *b* and *c* joining *a*'s household share a non-blank `householdId`).

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The change is coherent, additive, and idiomatic given this file's established conventions.

- **Logic is in the right unit (for this codebase):** `OwnerRestControllerV1` already houses the full family of owner-creation domain helpers as private methods — `generateCustomerCode`, `normalizeTelephone`/`toE164`, `normalizeEmail`, `requireUniqueTelephone`, `requireUniqueHousehold`, `normalizeForHousehold`. The new `joinHousehold`/`computeHouseholdId`/`findHouseholdMembers` sit naturally alongside those and follow the same shape, so a maintainer of this file would expect to find them exactly here.
- **Good deduplication:** extracting `findHouseholdMembers` and having both `requireUniqueHousehold` and `joinHousehold` call it removes what would otherwise be a duplicated `findAllOwners().stream()...normalizeForHousehold(...)` predicate. The old `anyMatch` inline logic is correctly collapsed into `!findHouseholdMembers(...).isEmpty()`.
- **The condition flip in `addOwner` is clean:** the `if (sharesHousehold) joinHousehold(owner); else requireUniqueHousehold(...)` branch reads clearly and keeps each path a single well-named call.
- **`computeHouseholdId` is a cohesive single-purpose helper.** Inlining `MessageDigest`/SHA-256 is slightly heavier than the other helpers, but it's a self-contained derivation with a clear contract and matches the file's practice of keeping such generation logic local (cf. `generateCustomerCode`). It reuses `normalizeForHousehold` so the identifier and the matching logic stay consistent.
- Schema/OpenAPI/model additions are the ordinary, parallel plumbing for a new field and are consistent across all four DB dialects plus the entity getter/setter and DTO doc.

No structural improvements needed.
